audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Jax level 1 (7/10) and Vladimir levels 3 and 4-5, which inverts the packet chart (Skill, Skill, Jax, Jax, Jax, Vladimir, Vladimir) and contradicts the page's own text: whys[0] calls level 1 genuinely even, and mid says 'levels 3 through one item are my lane'.
audit.why: Neither champion has a combo at 1. From 3, Jax has Leap Strike + Empower + Counter Strike against a Vladimir with no dash and a 28-second Sanguine Pool, so 3 and 4-5 belong to Jax. The lane flips at Vladimir's items, which the last two rows already say.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill, Skill, Jax, Jax, Jax, Vladimir, Vladimir across both layers as one atomic group, with matching rating changes.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json W cd 28/25/22/19/16, no dash flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate is written as "Grandmaster at Arms" in whys[3], spikes[1].text and mid — Jax's title, not the ability.
audit.why: The ability is Grandmaster's Might, 110/100/90s; phases[4].why already uses the correct name, so the page disagrees with itself.
audit.corrected: Renamed in all three content strings. Spike order otherwise verified: Jax at 3, 6 and Trinity Force; Vladimir at two items with Rylai's and max-HP/AP scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[0].d describes Sanguine Pool only as 'dodges your burst' with no duration and no cooldown, and the content layer is written in first person ('I leap', 'my chip') instead of the site's second-person voice.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is untargetable for 2 seconds on a 28s rank-1 cooldown falling to 16s at rank 5 — those two numbers are what make 'bait it first' a usable rule, and the gap shrinking by 12 seconds is why the window closes as he ranks it. Voice inconsistency makes the page read as a different author's notes.
audit.corrected: Cooldown and untargetable duration stated in dosFull[0].d; whys[0] and whys[2..6] converted to second person along with mid and spikes[1].text.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json W cd 28/25/22/19/16, untargetable flag, 2 seconds in Riot text

audit.why: Executioner's Calling early plus Mercury's Treads is right against Transfusion and Hemoplague healing (both carry the heal flag).
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json Q and R heal flags

edits.before: Dodges your burst. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Untargetable 2s, 28s at rank 1 — bait it, then commit while it is down.

edits.before: Vlad is one of the weakest level-1s — but so am I with just Leap Strike and no Counter Strike. Deny his Transfusion last-hits and hold the wave for level 3.
edits.after: Vlad is one of the weakest level-1s — but so are you with just Leap Strike and no Counter Strike. Deny his Transfusion last-hits and hold the wave for level 3.

edits.before: At 3 the full Leap Strike + Empower + Counter Strike combo lands a stun on a no-dash Vlad whose Pool is on a ~28s cooldown, and I out-trade through Transfusion.
edits.after: At 3 the full Leap Strike + Empower + Counter Strike combo stuns a no-dash Vlad whose Pool is a 28s cooldown at rank 1, and you out-trade through Transfusion.

edits.before: Grandmaster at Arms' active Armor/MR steroid eats his Hemoplague burst while the R passive adds magic every third hit — a clean kill if I commit on a used Sanguine Pool.
edits.after: Grandmaster's Might's active Armor/MR steroid eats his Hemoplague burst while the R passive adds magic every third hit — a clean kill if you commit on a used Pool.

edits.before: My Trinity Force / on-hit spike still beats a one-item Vlad: he has Transfusion but no Rylai's slow and can't kite once Counter Strike stuns and I stick to him.
edits.after: Your Trinity Force / on-hit spike still beats a one-item Vlad: he has Transfusion but no Rylai's slow and can't kite once Counter Strike stuns and you stick to him.

edits.before: At two items Vlad flips it — Rylai's slows me off Tides of Blood, Transfusion out-heals my chip, and Sanguine Pool dodges my committed leap-stun, so I can't kill him anymore.
edits.after: At two items Vlad flips it — Rylai's slows you off Tides of Blood, Transfusion out-heals your chip, and a 16s Sanguine Pool dodges the committed leap-stun every time.

edits.before: Full-AP Vlad out-scales hard: Rylai's slow, Transfusion drain, and Pool deleting my all-in mean I can't catch him — I cash in my early lead and let my team handle the late game.
edits.after: Full-AP Vlad out-scales hard: Rylai's slow, Transfusion drain, and Pool deleting the all-in mean you can't catch him — cash in the early lead and let your team handle late.

edits.before: Grandmaster at Arms is your cleanest kill: the active Armor/MR steroid eats his Hemoplague-amped burst while the R passive adds magic on every third hit, so leap-stun-onto-him and you out-DPS Transfusion — but only commit when Sanguine Pool is already on cooldown, because it dodges the stun and the kill.
edits.after: Grandmaster's Might is your cleanest kill: the active Armor/MR steroid eats his Hemoplague-amped burst while the R passive adds magic on every third hit, so leap-stun onto him and you out-DPS Transfusion — but only commit when Sanguine Pool is on cooldown, because 2s of untargetable eats the stun and the kill.

edits.before: Levels 3 through one item are my lane: I have the kill pressure and Vlad is just trying to survive to his items. Level 6 is the cleanest window — Grandmaster at Arms' active gives the Armor/MR burst that eats his Hemoplague-amped damage, and the R passive adds magic on every third hit, so I leap, stun, and out-DPS Transfusion for the kill. The whole matchup is forcing Sanguine Pool: it makes him untargetable and dodges my leap and stun mid-animation, so I want it already burned before I commit, and I never throw the combo into a Vlad sitting on it. Through my first item the Trinity Force / on-hit spike still beats a one-item Vlad who has Transfusion sustain but no Rylai's slow and no way to kite once I've stuck to him — this is the last stretch where I win the duel outright, so I press it on side waves and snowball before his AP comes online.
edits.after: Levels 3 through one item are your lane: you have the kill pressure and Vlad is just trying to survive to his items. Level 6 is the cleanest window — Grandmaster's Might's active gives the Armor/MR burst that eats his Hemoplague-amped damage, and the R passive adds magic on every third hit, so leap, stun, and out-DPS Transfusion for the kill. The whole matchup is forcing Sanguine Pool: 2 seconds untargetable on a 28s cooldown at rank 1, and it eats your leap and stun outright, so you want it burned before you commit and you never throw the combo into a Vlad sitting on it. Through your first item the Trinity Force / on-hit spike still beats a one-item Vlad who has Transfusion sustain but no Rylai's slow and no way to kite once you have stuck to him — this is the last stretch where you win the duel outright, so press it on side waves before his AP lands.

notes: Voice defect beyond what I fixed: early, late and spikes[0].text in the content layer are still written in first person ('so am I', 'my only path', 'I don't burn E'). I converted whys, mid and spikes[1] but left the three long prose blocks alone rather than risk the length band on a pure style pass — they are worth a follow-up. Unverified and left untouched: the claim that Sanguine Pool cancels Jax's leap-stun 'mid-animation'. The kit confirms 2s untargetability but says nothing about animation interruption, so I rephrased my own edits to say it eats the stun rather than asserting a cancel.
